movie.title: It Ends
movie.overview: A group of recent grads head out on a late night drive for grub, hoping to enjoy one final hangout before their paths diverge. Instead, they accidentally turn onto a never-ending, two-lane hellscape surrounded by untold horrors and cosmic forces beyond their understanding. Cramped together inside a Jeep Cherokee and with the miles stretching infinitely ahead, they face a choice: embrace their new existence or fight to escape it.

reviews.author: Sierbahnn
reviews.content:
Open wide and still claustrophobic
It is a bit strange how an open road can feel claustrophobic, but it does.

It is a well acted movie, and while the plot is only there to allow for character exploration, and you never truly get to learn a whole lot about the actual setting, that's part of the idea. Resolutions are optional in such stories.

The movie is by no means bad, but it is not one I will revisit and rewatch.

reviews.author: Brent Marchant
reviews.content: In the interest of full disclosure up front, I’ll do my best to assess this release without being overly unkind. To be honest, this debut feature from writer-director Alexander Ullom has almost assuredly earned itself a spot on my “Worst of 2026” list. Loosely based on the 1944 existentialist stage play *No Exit* by Jean-Paul Sartre, “It Ends” tells the story of four twenty-something friends (a term I use loosely) (Phinehas Yoon, Mitchell Cole, Akira Jackson, Noah Toth) who embark on a late-night drive but soon find themselves lost on a never-ending highway through a thickly forested woodland from which there’s no apparent escape (*i.e.*, “no exit”). In an effort to spice up the plot, the narrative subsequently attempts to infuse a few horror tropes, but, sadly, these poorly handled elements aren’t particularly scary or the least bit enlightening in defining the essence of the plot. (At one point, for instance, the puzzled quartet is attacked by a band of fleet-footed zombies, forcing the fearful foursome to flee for their lives. It’s an element that’s reincorporated or inferred throughout the film but that, frankly, has little ultimate bearing on the story. What’s more, the sequence is so ineptly executed that it’s ultimately more confusing than frightening.) Not long thereafter, when matters settle down and these lost souls begin discussing the nature of their bewildering circumstances, they’re forced to begin considering that they might be trapped in some kind of alternate existence, even a hellish version of the afterlife. That possibility, in turn, prompts yet another round of long-winded, uninteresting existential discussions that are part metaphysics, part petty bickering and part overwrought Generation Z angst, all set against the backdrop of an incessant road trip for which practical concerns like having enough fuel for the journey (wherever it may be headed) are apparently irrelevant. And that, in a nutshell, fittingly characterizes the dynamics of this wholly pretentious offering, despite what may have started out with a worthwhile premise and good intentions. The blame here lies largely with the woefully undercooked, meandering screenplay. For example, most of the excessive group discussions are lame and unfocused and lack engaging substance, light years removed from the eloquence and insight of the source material that inspired this production. Then there’s the seriously underused horror aspect, which might have added more interest if more skillfully and integrally employed. The filming techniques are also stunningly puzzling, with much of the action shot too dimly and/or too up-close, so much so that, in sequences like the zombie attack, it’s difficult to tell what’s happening. And, of course, there are plot holes aplenty, which are genuinely inexcusable, even for a first-time filmmaker. To its credit, though, the picture gets one thing right: it’s a testament to Sartre’s renowned contention that “hell is other people,” as these characters come to find out for themselves, bringing fresh meaning to that statement and to the audience (indeed, I can’t imagine being stuck with individuals like these for eternity; 89 minutes was more than enough for me). But that spot-on irony is not nearly enough to save this effort, especially since it even more ironically gives viewers reason to skip this release. Perhaps, as a senior, the generational nuances at work here were lost on me, but, that aside, while screening this offering, I also couldn’t help but keep asking myself, “Are we there yet?”

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: A group of recent graduates on a late-night food run finds themselves trapped inside a Jeep on a stretching, two-lane highway surrounded by supernatural and cosmic horrors.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Hoping for one final hangout before parting ways, a group of recent college graduates embarks on a late-night drive to grab food. Their casual night takes a terrifying turn when they inadvertently turn onto a endless, two-lane road that defies the laws of physics. Cramped inside their Jeep Cherokee and surrounded by incomprehensible cosmic forces, they are forced to confront untold terrifying threats. As the infinite miles stretch ahead, the friends must decide whether to fight for a way out or accept their surreal new reality.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Following their graduation, a tight-knit group of friends decides to embark on a late-night drive to grab a quick bite and celebrate one last memory together before life takes them in different directions. The casual outing takes a dark and inexplicable turn when they make a wrong turn onto an isolated, two-lane road. They quickly realize this is no ordinary stretch of highway, as their surroundings morph into a surreal, inescapable hellscape governed by incomprehensible cosmic entities. Trapped within the confines of a Jeep Cherokee, panic sets in as the odometer ticks away while the road stretches infinitely into the void. Surrounding them in the darkness are terrifying forces that test their sanity, their bonds, and their understanding of existence. Confined to the small cabin, interpersonal drama and unspoken tensions resurface as the oppressive environment weighs heavily on their psyches. With no turns, exits, or end in sight, the group is forced to navigate both the grotesque horrors outside and the fractured dynamics within. Ultimately, as their hope diminishes against the infinite landscape, they face a harrowing ultimatum: surrender to the dark logic of this never-ending dimension or risk everything to claw their way back to reality.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: It Ends is an intense horror-drama that follows a group of recent graduates attempting to enjoy one final late-night outing together before embarking on their separate paths in life. What begins as an innocent drive for food devolves into a terrifying ordeal when they turn onto a dark, endless stretch of highway. Confined inside a Jeep Cherokee, the friends find themselves trapped in a surreal, infinite hellscape plagued by mind-bending cosmic horrors. As psychological tension rises inside the vehicle and inexplicable terrors loom outside, the group must grapple with unknown forces and choose whether to accept their strange new nightmare or fight to find an exit.
